# Psychological Safety

## R36 — Retro on Retros

- **Canvas and timebox:** 4 Quadrants: Format, Psychological Safety, Action Velocity, Value · 60 min
- **When to run it:** Retrospective meetings have become stale, mechanical, or cynical; participants report low return on investment and action items are ignored.
- **Phases:**
  - Set the stage (5m): recite the Prime Directive; name past ceremony failures.
  - Gather data (15m): anonymously rate safety and action velocity, 1 to 5.
  - Generate insights (20m): find why retros stall; name the common antipatterns.
  - Decide (15m): redesign the cadence; rotation, frequency, WIP limits.
  - Close (5m): re-commit to collective continuous improvement.
- **The move:** Actions reform the improvement process itself: rotate the facilitator and cap process tickets with a WIP limit.
- **Provenance:** Source protocol: the phases and minutes follow the written sequence in the source.
- **Source:** The source names no originator.

## R37 — Team Health Radar

- **Canvas and timebox:** 6 Dimensions: Code Health, Delivery, Fun, Safety, Autonomy, Speed · 60 min
- **When to run it:** Teams needing a holistic, multi-dimensional health assessment beyond velocity and bug counts.
- **Phases:**
  - Set the stage (10m): explain the six dimensions and the 1-to-5 scale.
  - Gather data (15m): anonymous poll on all six dimensions.
  - Generate insights (15m): plot the median; name the lowest and most split.
  - Decide (10m): pick the lowest dimension for a month-long initiative.
  - Close (10m): set the re-poll date and the owner.
- **The move:** The lowest-scoring dimension becomes a focused improvement initiative for the upcoming month, with an owner and a re-poll date.
- **Provenance:** Source names the canvas and the intent and leaves the phases' wording and minutes to the facilitator.
- **Source:** The source names no originator.

## R38 — Working Agreement Audit

- **Canvas and timebox:** 3 Columns: Existing Agreement, Reality Check, Ratified Rules · 60–90 min
- **When to run it:** Broken team norms, recurring PR review bottlenecks, off-hours messaging, or boundary violations.
- **Phases:**
  - Set the stage (10m): list the agreements the team actually made.
  - Gather data (20m): mark where each agreement is followed or ignored.
  - Generate insights (25m): separate silent drift from rules that no longer work.
  - Decide (15m): drop, re-commit, or automate each agreement.
  - Close (10m): commit the revised agreements to the repository.
- **The move:** Revised agreements land in /docs/working-agreements.md with automated enforcement where chosen.
- **Provenance:** Source names the canvas and the intent and leaves the phases' wording and minutes to the facilitator.
- **Source:** The source names no originator.

## R39 — Toxic Waste Dump

- **Canvas and timebox:** 3 Sequestered Zones: Containment Trench, Decontamination, Clean Ground · 60–90 min
- **When to run it:** Severe post-crunch burnout, organizational trauma, executive conflict, or high interpersonal frustration.
- **Phases:**
  - Set the stage (10m): Prime Directive; containment rules; no personal attacks.
  - Gather data (20m): total silence; post frustrations into the Containment Trench.
  - Generate insights (25m): read notes without defence; sort reality from friction.
  - Decide (15m): pick exactly one systemic issue to neutralize.
  - Close (10m): shred the trench notes; confirm mutual support.
- **The move:** Extracted friction becomes a protective barrier ticket: no-meeting Wednesdays for four weeks, with an owner.
- **Provenance:** Source protocol: the phases and minutes follow the written sequence in the source.
- **Source:** The source names no originator.

## R40 — ESVP Safety Baseline

- **Canvas and timebox:** 4 Anonymous Buckets: Explorer, Shopper, Vacationer, Prisoner · 15–20 min
- **When to run it:** Noticeable disengagement, passive-aggressive silence, or when facilitating a newly formed team.
- **Phases:**
  - Set the stage (3m): explain the four buckets.
  - Gather data (4m): silently pick Explorer, Shopper, Vacationer, or Prisoner.
  - Generate insights (5m): tally publicly; if Vacationers and Prisoners exceed half, pause.
  - Decide (5m): with low safety, switch to a root-cause session on autonomy.
  - Close (3m): name the one condition that would raise safety next time.
- **The move:** If low safety is uncovered, the retro becomes a root-cause session on organizational autonomy, with a follow-up date.
- **Provenance:** Source names the canvas and the intent and leaves the phases' wording and minutes to the facilitator.
- **Source:** Esther Derby & Diana Larsen (2006), *Agile Retrospectives*.

## R41 — Circles and Soup (CIA)

- **Canvas and timebox:** 3 Concentric Circles: Control, Influence, The Soup · 60 min
- **When to run it:** Teams trapped in learned helplessness, complaining about executive decisions or external dependencies beyond their control.
- **Phases:**
  - Set the stage (10m): draw the three circles.
  - Gather data (15m): write every complaint and challenge on a note.
  - Generate insights (15m): place each note; test the Soup items for influence.
  - Decide (10m): convert Control and Influence items into backlog tickets.
  - Close (10m): write adaptation protocols for what stays in The Soup.
- **The move:** Only Control and Influence notes become backlog tickets; Soup notes generate internal resilience protocols.
- **Provenance:** Source names the canvas and the intent and leaves the phases' wording and minutes to the facilitator.
- **Source:** Henri Lipmanowicz & Keith McCandless (2013), *The Surprising Power of Liberating Structures*.

## R42 — TRIZ (Destructive Innovation)

- **Canvas and timebox:** 3 Phases: Maximum Sabotage, Brutal Reality, Firebreak Actions · 75 min
- **When to run it:** Complacency, repeated missed sprint goals, or teams resistant to traditional process retrospectives.
- **Phases:**
  - Set the stage (10m): explain the joke; brainstorm how to guarantee failure.
  - Gather data (15m): list the worst practices in Phase 1.
  - Generate insights (25m): confront reality; tick what the team tolerates.
  - Decide (15m): turn each tick into a Stop Doing agreement.
  - Close (10m): name the first practice to stop this sprint.
- **The move:** Checkmarked sabotage behaviors become explicit Stop Doing agreements with an owner and a start date.
- **Provenance:** Source names the canvas and the intent and leaves the phases' wording and minutes to the facilitator.
- **Source:** Genrich Altshuller (1984), *Creativity as an Exact Science*. Henri Lipmanowicz & Keith McCandless (2013), *The Surprising Power of Liberating Structures*.

## R43 — 1-2-4-All Systemic Sync

- **Canvas and timebox:** 4 Sequential Workspaces: 1-min Solo, 2-min Pair, 4-min Quad, Plenary · 30–45 min
- **When to run it:** Retrospectives dominated by senior engineers, architects, or managers, where junior and introverted team members remain silent.
- **Phases:**
  - Set the stage (5m): pose the question; explain the four stages.
  - Gather data (10m): 1 minute solo, 2 minutes in pairs, 4 minutes in fours.
  - Generate insights (10m): harvest patterns; each group names its strongest idea.
  - Decide (10m): submit each group's insight to the Who-What-When converter.
  - Close (5m): read commitments; set the next review.
- **The move:** Each group of four submits its highest-leverage insight as a dated commitment with a named owner.
- **Provenance:** Source names the canvas and the intent and leaves the phases' wording and minutes to the facilitator.
- **Source:** Henri Lipmanowicz & Keith McCandless (2013), *The Surprising Power of Liberating Structures*.

## R44 — Appreciation Matrix & Kudos

- **Canvas and timebox:** Grid Layout: Core Peer Categories (Heroics, Glue-Work, Empathy, Mentorship) · 30–45 min
- **When to run it:** Teams recovering from sustained deadlines, high-stress delivery cycles, or transactional working relationships.
- **Phases:**
  - Set the stage (5m): explain the four appreciation categories.
  - Gather data (10m): write at least two specific kudos to peers.
  - Generate insights (10m): read the notes aloud; name the repeated behaviours.
  - Decide (5m): copy the appreciations into the public channel.
  - Close (5m): commit to one recognition habit for the next sprint.
- **The move:** Appreciations are copied into the organization's public channel, giving the work company-wide visibility.
- **Provenance:** Source names the canvas and the intent and leaves the phases' wording and minutes to the facilitator.
- **Source:** The source names no originator.

## R45 — Role & Decision Matrix (D3)

- **Canvas and timebox:** 3 Operational Tiers: Do, Discuss, Decide · 60 min
- **When to run it:** Friction over code reviews, ambiguous PR approvals, overlapping responsibilities, or micro-management disputes.
- **Phases:**
  - Set the stage (10m): draw roles across, Do, Discuss and Decide down.
  - Gather data (15m): each role writes what others should Do, Discuss, Decide.
  - Generate insights (15m): compare perceptions with the actual role-holders.
  - Decide (10m): resolve each boundary mismatch into one owner.
  - Close (10m): export the consensus as the team decision governance doc.
- **The move:** The resolved consensus is exported as a governance document and committed to the repository.
- **Provenance:** Source names the canvas and the intent and leaves the phases' wording and minutes to the facilitator.
- **Source:** The source names no originator.
